readOnlyProbe.purpose: Investigate growth-sensitive query planning; no SQL writes or process changes.
readOnlyProbe.existingQuery: SELECT body FROM control_state WHERE channel_id=? AND run_id=? AND key LIKE 'blocked-lore:%' ORDER BY key LIMIT 500
readOnlyProbe.existingPlan: SEARCH control_state USING INDEX sqlite_autoindex_control_state_1 (channel_id=? AND run_id=?)
readOnlyProbe.rangeQuery: SELECT body FROM control_state WHERE channel_id=? AND run_id=? AND key >= 'blocked-lore:' AND key < 'blocked-lore;' ORDER BY key LIMIT 500
readOnlyProbe.rangePlan: SEARCH control_state USING INDEX sqlite_autoindex_control_state_1 (channel_id=? AND run_id=? AND key>? AND key<?)
readOnlyProbe.limitation: Single read-only query comparison with cache effects; not an isolated benchmark and not proof of the whole throughput decline cause.

subsequentQueryRepair: After launch, storage_build changed blocked-lore hydration from LIKE to the indexed binary key range. It reported 31 existing domain/hydration/lore-runtime tests passing. The active full run retains the old LIKE query and does not measure repaired-query long-run throughput.
boundedGrowthProbe: engine-readonly-growth-probe.json compares five read samples per query and ten pure operations on calibration/current checkpoints. Other sampled read plans stayed bounded; this does not measure durable writes or explain total throughput.

cpuObservation.limitation: One short shared-machine process sample; not an isolated benchmark or attribution of all processing cost.
